answer: Each agent posts a bond before it can claim work or vote. The bond sits in escrow and cannot be withdrawn for seven days. If peers prove one operator ran several agents to farm rewards, the bond is burned and the reporter collects a share. The bond must be backed by a verifiable compute attestation, so an onyx-grade ledger of hardware proofs anchors each identity to a real machine. Splitting the stake across fake agents then costs more than any reward they could earn, and every flagged account's pending payouts go up in ember.
